pages.title: AI Captions
pages.description: Complete reference for local Whisper models, audio sources, downloads, transcription, regeneration, cancellation, and diagnostics.
pages.lead: Beam generates speech captions locally from an enabled audio clip. It downloads the selected Whisper model, transcribes on the device, and creates editable caption clips on the timeline.

screenshot.alt: Beam AI Captions panel with audio source and Whisper model controls
screenshot.caption: Select an enabled audio source and a local Whisper model before generating captions.

sections.title: Generate and regenerate
steps: Choose one of the enabled audio sources.
Choose and download a Whisper model if it is not ready.
Select Generate Captions. Beam decodes the source, converts it to mono 16 kHz audio, and limits it to the timeline duration.
Partial transcription results update the composition while processing continues.
The completed run selects the first generated caption for editing.

rows: Ends a caption phrase at punctuation or after 12 words.
Replaces existing AI-generated captions and preserves manual captions.
Reports elapsed time and exposes a copyable transcription report after processing.

notice.title: Local transcription
notice.text: Whisper runs on the device. Caption generation does not require a cloud upload or API key.

sections.title: Edit generated captions
paragraphs: Generated captions are regular editable caption clips marked as AI-generated. Their text, timing, and visual style can be adjusted through the Clip panel and timeline after generation.

pages.title: Audio
pages.description: Complete reference for global output, system and microphone roles, imported audio, enable states, deletion, and volume.
pages.lead: The Audio panel separates composition-wide output from recorded system and microphone roles. Imported audio remains controlled as a selected timeline clip.

screenshot.alt: Beam Audio panel with global, system, and microphone volume controls
screenshot.caption: Global output and recorded audio roles can be adjusted independently.

sections.title: Enable compared with delete
paragraphs: Disabling a role preserves its clips but excludes them from playback and export. Deleting a role removes every clip assigned to that role from the composition.

notice.title: Role deletion affects multiple clips
notice.text: Delete System Track and Delete Microphone Track operate on the complete role, not only the clip nearest the playhead.

sections.title: Dev Mode
paragraphs: Dev Mode is stored locally in the editor. It is intended for development and troubleshooting rather than normal editing.
